findings.title: req.destroy() right after writing 413 can reset the socket before the response flushes
findings.evidence: res.status(413).json({ error: "request body too large" }); followed synchronously by req.destroy();
findings.recommendation: Do not call req.destroy() synchronously after writing the response. Either respond and let the connection close normally, pause/unpipe the stream and drain it, or destroy the socket only after the response finishes (e.g. inside res.on('finish')/res.end callback / req.res 'close').

findings.title: Content-type check is a loose prefix match, accepting non-JSON media types
findings.evidence: if (!contentType.toLowerCase().startsWith("application/json")) accepts application/jsonp, application/json-evil, application/jsonfoo, etc.
findings.recommendation: Parse the media type (split on ';', trim) and compare the base type exactly to 'application/json' (optionally allow a whitelist of +json types) rather than using startsWith.

findings.title: No handling for client abort before end, request may stall without next/res
findings.evidence: Only data/end/error listeners are registered; a client that closes mid-body emitting 'aborted'/'close' without a subsequent 'end' or 'error' leaves the middleware unsettled, so next()/res is never invoked for that request.
findings.recommendation: Add a req.on('aborted') / req.on('close') handler (or rely on req 'error' with premature-close) to settle the request and clear the settled flag once, guarding against double-invocation.
